SUMO-1 modification is associated with transcriptional activation, whereas SUMO-2 modification is linked to repression, thus suggesting that SUMOylation is an important epigenetic mechanism for regulating the expression of key immune-related gene during herpesvirus infection.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SUMO-1 modification is not required during KSHV reactivations and the presence of SUMO-2 and/or SUMO-3 at promoters is sufficient to maintain the transcriptional status of immune-related genes.

the chromatin modification by K-bZIP and SUMO-1/2/3 plays a role in the transcriptional regulation of immune-related genes during viral reactivation, which is important for viral persistence and pathogenesis.

The main takeaway from our work is that
SUMOylation can be used by viruses as a mechanism to prevent the activation of host genes involved in the immune response.
the SUMOylation of host immune response genes by KSHV is a potential mechanism for the virus to escape immune surveillance.
